## Identity

## Biography

"I specialise in curiosity."

My creative pursuits started with copying comic book characters in my primary school homework notebooks and dreaming of working for Cartoon Network on series like Cow and Chicken, Dexter's Laboratory, and I Am Weasel. In early teens, I was designing pixel art on my Nokia 3310 and digitally composing my friends into surreal collages using a pirated copy of Paint Shop Pro 8.

In my late teens, I made stencil art, spent time in a darkroom developing film photography, acted in a local theatre group, and designed nightclub posters. In my early 20s, I ran a tattoo parlour in my living room, gave my mum her first tattoo, and had my design work in 400+ tech stores across the UK before I landed my first full-time job in the creative industry.

For the past 15 years, I've been blessed to work across brand identity, commercial art direction, digital experiences, packaging design, video production, print publications, illustration and interactive media.

In 2019, I co-founded Daydream Believers (https://daydreambelievers.co.uk/), helping build it into an award-winning educational organisation recognised as one of the top 100 education innovators in the world by HundrED, working in partnership with LEGO, Rockstar North, D&AD, and the Ellen MacArthur Foundation.

In 2021, I founded Calumma (https://calumma.design/), a creative studio for rebellious-optimist-led organisations tackling challenges across education, healthcare, tech, and environmental conservation.

Born in Latvia, became a professional adult in Scotland, and currently raising three wonderfully wild children in northern Portugal while constantly getting lost in weird rabbit holes of information about our complex life in this corner of the universe.

---

## Career History

### Calumma — Co-Founder & Creative Director
Period: November 2021 – Present

Founded a brand communications studio that works exclusively with organisations tackling important challenges across education, healthcare, environmental conservation, and emerging technology. Leading all creative output, client relationships, and studio direction from day one. It operates as a small distributed practice with collaborators across Europe and North America, providing solutions for branding, educational content, film, web design, copywriting, and communication strategy.

Notable clients: John Muir Trust · Oxfam Denmark · Glasgow School of Art · AHIMA Foundation · BIMA · Education Scotland · Georgetown University · Femern A/S · Lung Ambition Alliance · YESfest · Frontier Films · Mercurial AI

---

### Daydream Believers — Co-Founder & Design Director
Period: April 2019 – February 2025

Helped build Daydream Believers from a grassroots idea into an award-winning organisation recognised as one of the top 100 education innovators in the world by HundrED. Led brand strategy, design direction, and the creation of 30+ interactive learning resources reaching 50,000+ students globally — covering topics from the circular economy and biomimicry to cybersecurity, GenAI, and mental health. The work eventually supported the launch of an accredited Creative Thinking qualification in the Scottish education system.

Notable collaborators: LEGO · D&AD · Ellen MacArthur Foundation · Rockstar North · Education Scotland · Dentsu Creative · WPP · Adidas · PechaKucha

---

### Humanize — Lead Designer
Period: October 2022 – December 2023

Designed the user experience and interface for a science-backed mental wellness platform built around partner-based empathy practices developed by Prof. Dr. Tania Singer of the Max Planck Society. Led a cross-functional team through the development of a mobile app and web-based platform — from scheduling infrastructure to live session tools — finishing with a 4.8/5 user satisfaction rating and lasting impact on their ability to be compassionate to others.

---

### Goodfuse — Creative Director
Period: July 2020 – April 2021

Embedded as a fully remote creative director for a New York-based agency specialising in human-centred healthcare communications. Led branding and web design projects aimed at bringing clarity and genuine empathy into an industry not always known for either. Worked primarily with pharma and health advocacy clients across the US.

Notable clients: Pfizer · AstraZeneca · GCI Health · Novocure · Cancer Support Community · YouthBuild USA · IONIS · Lung Ambition Alliance

---

### Campfire — Designer & Art Director
Period: December 2016 – May 2019

Led design and art direction with a small ragtag creative team at an independent Edinburgh studio, doing everything from whisky brand films and hospitality experiences to experimental live musical events. Produced notable work across film, digital, and print, and once got invited to attend a dinner with Leonardo DiCaprio, organised by Sir Tom Hunter.

Notable clients: Bunnahabhain Distillery · Deanston Distillery · Hard Rock Hotels · Medtronic · Diageo · Edrington · RBS · Startup Summit

---

### Daily Haloha — UX & Graphic Designer
Period: October 2018 – March 2019

A short but focused initial engagement designing the full user experience for an anonymous self-reflection and empathy app ahead of its global iOS and Android launch, which later evolved into continuous support and design assistance for future updates over the years — a useful lesson in building something intimate and intentional from scratch under a tight deadline and then continuing to craft it without losing the core value and authenticity.

---

### Whitespace — Designer
Period: June 2014 – May 2016

First official full-time role, working across graphic design, digital, animation, and interactive experiences for a range of public sector and commercial clients. Designed an award-winning Oxfam website that got cancelled by the internet. Also, out of selfish reasons, promoted cross-team collaboration to avoid outsourcing creativity on client projects, and convinced leadership to invest in further-learning opportunities for creatives to attend global conferences.

Notable clients: Oxfam GB · VisitScotland · National Museum of Scotland · Scottish Enterprise · RBS · Road Safety Scotland · Business Gateway

---

### Freelance & Upskilling — Designer, Photographer & Experimenter
Period: 2008 – 2014

The years of experimentation, upskilling, and pivoting — wedding photography, nightclub posters, custom illustrations, street art, tattooing, Society6 apparel design, and small business branding executed with cracked software on Windows 7. During this time, relocated from Latvia to Scotland and completed an HND in Visual Communication at Edinburgh College, where a student competition entry turned into a product range sold in 400+ Dixons, Currys, and PC World stores across the UK.

## Selected Client Work

Full portfolio at https://emilblum.com/featured

### Hard Rock Hotel
URL: https://emilblum.com/featured/hard-rock-hotel
Disciplines: Craft, Product Design, Packaging, Experiential
Subtitle: A paper vinyl record player, custom-pressed and made from scratch in ten days.

Challenge: I needed to produce ten functional paper record players, designed and produced from scratch, to be in guests' hotel rooms in Tenerife within ten days. There was no template, no prior experience making anything like it, no existing supplier chain, and no margin for a second attempt.

Approach: Working backwards from the deadline, I sourced a small UK vinyl presser, got musician Richard Jahn to donate a track, and folded stacks of paper prototypes testing needle types and their potential for audible sound. Antique gramophone needles and custom-cut bamboo chopsticks turned out to be the right combination.

Outcome: Ten complete paper record players with individually customised vinyls — recorded, designed, hand-assembled, folded, and packaged through several intense days and nights — arrived in guests' rooms alongside flowers and merch. The influencers filmed and shared videos of themselves playing with the gifts on socials. The client was happy and I could finally take a nap.

---

### Daydream Believers
URL: https://emilblum.com/featured/daydream-believers
Disciplines: Brand Identity, Illustration, Web Design, Educational Content
Subtitle: A rebrand built to grow an innovative educational platform from grassroots idea to globally recognised organisation.

Challenge: The brand needed to speak to two very different audiences simultaneously — teachers looking for credible curriculum tools, and young people who needed a reason to engage. One visual language with the ability to inspire and stand the test of time.

Approach: We chose to embrace the messy creative process and give the brand a character both big and small could engage with. We leaned into a layered and vibrant visual language filled with scribbles and mixed-media collages, accompanied by a new brand mascot — Brua, an illustrated cloud named after the Scottish Gaelic word "Bruadarach" meaning dreamer or visionary. In addition to a new tone of voice and a custom-built website, over 40 unique collages were created as resource thumbnails, giving each learning resource its own distinct visual character.

Outcome: The rebrand supported the launch of an accredited Creative Thinking Qualification in the Scottish education system, opened countless doors to new partnerships (LEGO, Ellen MacArthur Foundation, Rockstar North, Skyscanner, D&AD), and helped Daydream Believers reach 50,000+ students globally. In 2023, the organisation was recognised as one of the top 100 education innovators in the world by HundrED.

### Stewart Brewing
URL: https://emilblum.com/featured/stewart-brewing
Disciplines: Packaging, 3D Visuals, Augmented Reality, Brand Identity
Subtitle: Beer labels designed from the inside out to present the hidden elements of craft in each brew.

Challenge: Each beer in the series is entirely distinct — different ingredients, different processes, different character. The packaging needed a visual system flexible enough to give each beer its own identity while still reading as a coherent series on shelf.

Approach: We looked closely at the process and chose to visualise the microscopic elements and the secret ingredients that make each beer special — the Elements of Craft. Each beer's ingredients and process were translated into a unique 3D molecular form — inspired by medical imaging and microscopic organisms. An AR app extended the idea further: point your phone at the can, summon the element, and explore it in your own space.

Outcome: The system proved extensible by design — as new beers joined the series, new elements were created to match the flavours, the ingredients and the character of each beer. The project won Best Concept Design at the SIBA Business Awards 2019, recognising both the packaging concept and the AR experience as an authentic celebration of the beer brewing craft. Over the course of our partnership, we developed labels for 19 different beers that helped establish Stewart Brewing as true champions of the craft with thousands of new fans.

---

### FISGA Spaces
URL: https://emilblum.com/featured/fisga
Disciplines: Brand Identity, Web Design, Print, Digital
Subtitle: A modular identity for a Porto creative hub that refuses to stand still.

Challenge: There was no existing brand, just a bunch of on-the-fly communication assets created by various team members over the previous two years since the start of the project. With offerings so diverse across two completely different locations — desk spaces, art exhibitions, film nights, summer jams, corporate workshops, and community programming — the brand also needed to be flexible. One visual system needed to hold all of it without feeling like a compromise in any direction.

Approach: A modular system was built around an open, reconfigurable geometric mark symbolising a three-dimensional letter "F", providing a form that can uniquely adapt to create distinct marks for each current and future location. These were accompanied by their own primary colour inspired by the character of the space — Warehouse in electric blue and Garden in sunny yellow. The web design, developed in partnership with Unset Studio, extended the brand into a full digital platform, with custom booking system and event calendar.

Outcome: The identity launched alongside the new space and has continued to evolve with the organisation, extending into wayfinding, signage, merchandise and social content without strain. The new branding, and the community it attracted, have helped Fisga become a member of the European Creative Hubs Network and establish itself as one of Porto's most recognisable and celebrated creative spaces.

---

### Unseen
URL: https://emilblum.com/featured/unseen
Disciplines: Campaign, Digital, Interactive, Web Design, Print
Subtitle: A social awareness campaign centred on a 360° immersive experience that places the viewer inside the world of a child living with abuse.

Challenge: Policymakers had seen the statistics and were familiar with the realities of children living in an abusive environment. Yet most of them hadn't experienced the weight of that life — the isolation, fear, unpredictability, emotional turmoil — so they had other plans for the funding money. Our work needed to change their minds.

Approach: With the help of Perry Jonsson and actors from spoken word collective Loud Poets, we produced a series of videos stitched together in 360° format for viewing on a VR headset, with headphones playing increasingly distorting audio to heighten the emotional unease. Alongside the video, I art directed the ominous brand photography, designed the brand identity, and built the website as an informational hub for the campaign and a guide to available social services.

Outcome: The experience premiered at the charity's headquarters in Scotland to a large crowd of politicians and council members, with great emotional impact and later showcased on YouTube and 360° video platforms where it reached new support. The campaign was recognised as one of Scotland's 100 Disruptors by The Hunter Foundation in 2018. Unfortunately, none of that was enough to save the charity from closure — a hard lesson in how the work can land exactly right, yet the cause it's fighting for can still be lost.

---

### National Museum of Scotland — Game Masters
URL: https://emilblum.com/featured/game-masters
Disciplines: Campaign, Illustration, Print, Digital
Subtitle: A campaign for the first European showing of Game Masters that drew 65,000 visitors — 58% of whom had never attended a special exhibition at the museum before.

Challenge: The exhibition's real subject — the designers behind decades of beloved games — wasn't an obvious crowd-puller on its own. The design needed to make gaming feel culturally significant, not just nostalgic, to an audience well beyond the converted.

Approach: A grid system inspired by circuit boards — the architecture that makes games run — became the campaign's visual foundation. Iconic gaming characters were reconstructed within it as neon circuit illustrations, creating a system that scaled from outdoor posters to exhibition walls to museum merchandise.

Outcome: The campaign drew 65,000 visitors, with 58% having never attended a special exhibition at the museum before, proving especially popular with men and younger audiences. It won the Scottish Creative Awards 2015 for Use of Visual Design.

---

### Oxfam — Republic of You
URL: https://emilblum.com/featured/oxfam-republic-of-you
Disciplines: Game Design, Interactive, Illustration, Web Design, Campaign
Subtitle: A retro-gaming-inspired political quiz giving anyone a chance to step into the shoes of a national leader.

Challenge: Inequality is easy to care about in theory and easy to ignore in practice. The challenge was making policy feel personally consequential — without being preachy or academic — to an audience that would usually avoid the subject altogether.

Approach: Working closely with illustrator Katie McPherson and a team of copywriters, UX designers and developers, we created a retro web-based 8-bit game built around a set of deterministic questions about national policy — where every leadership decision about healthcare, wages, wealth tax and social services shaped a personalised country landscape, triggered citizen reactions, and linked directly to real Oxfam case studies about global equivalents.

Outcome: The game received a Commendation at the Scottish Design Awards 2016 and inspired Oxfam to pursue more interactive campaigns to further their work, but it also received a fair dose of criticism from the public for oversimplifying the causes of inequality and was eventually shut down. In the years that followed, the political landscape made it look considerably less oversimplified.

## Code & Tools

Full list at https://emilblum.com/code

Heading on the page: "LLM-assisted coding experiments and tools."

- (Mind)Space — https://x.com/emilblum/status/2057472892699361747
  An experiment-in-process — locally hosted project management and creative process canvas tool built to help see everything in-progress at the same time, without navigating through folders. Includes automatic launches of local servers for dev projects, local Whisper speech-to-text model integration for notes, and many other features.

- Vault of Vör — https://vor.emilblum.com/
  Began as a fascination with steganography after learning it's possible to hide text and audio in the pixels of an image. Lets you upload any image and encode secret messages within it with military-grade security. Useful for encoding memories in photos or sharing messages as a whistleblower to journalists.

- 3DGS Forest Bathing — https://forest.emilblum.com/
  An experimental website created to test 3D Gaussian Splat embedding on an educational website. Only fully functional on desktop due to the heavy 3D splat file.

- Reveil — https://reveil.emilblum.com/
  An experimental awareness tool for discovering how much information your device, browser, and computer automatically broadcast for anyone to see, if they wish. Plus additional face and audio recognition visualisers.

- Page Runner — https://page-runner.emilblum.com/
  Speed-reading tool based on the Optimal Recognition Point concept, first introduced by Frank Waldman's Spritz app. Useful for reading .md, .txt, and .docx files.

- Gradient Tool — https://gradient.emilblum.com/
  A simple tool for creating gradients, built to replace frustrating Adobe CC gradient workflows.

- Sound.img — https://sound-img.emilblum.com/
  Maps pixel colour values to musical notes and sounds for endless procedural music-making from images.

- Window to Nature — https://window.calumma.design/
  Part Pomodoro Technique-based focus tool, part an attempt to be reminded there is more to life past the office walls and the computer screen.
